requests.anchor: SL-23 (2): "The write is issued at the staging step of the `DEAD` boundary (or of the load), runs while the kernel is in `LOADING`, and the end-of-`LOADING` hand-off (T-8 step 7, K-4, provisional) waits for its `EPOCH_DURABLE` report"
requests.change: Rewrite SL-23 from "Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling R1 (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): **Save/Load owns `restore_epoch`**" through "The former rule \"advances on a death-stub restore only\" is superseded by (1)." as follows (keep (3) and (4) as they are): "Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling R1, as amended 2026-10-28 by delegated rulings R13 and R14 (user delegated all remaining calls): **Save/Load owns `restore_epoch`**, a persisted unsigned 32-bit integer that starts at 0 at `new_game` (SL-18). (0) *Storage (R14).* It lives in the per-slot side file `slot_epoch.bin` (SL-19): the u32, little-endian, followed by its CRC32, written by the Save/Load worker as `slot_epoch.bin.tmp`, flushed, re-read, CRC-checked and renamed over `slot_epoch.bin`. It is in no generation file, so no generation's bytes, trailer SHA-256, `state_hash` or any key derived from them (SL-12's REBASED baseline key included) ever change after the generation is written. Every generation header records the value live at write time (SL-1, a read-only copy, never rewritten). The value is read once when the campaign is opened (T-6) and held in memory. A missing `slot_epoch.bin`, or one whose CRC fails, reads as `max(restore_epoch of the newest generation's header copy, 0) + 1`, newest by header `generation` among the files that pass the file stage. (1) *When it advances (R13).* A death-stub restore (`DEATH_STUB`), a `FAULT_RECOVERY`, and a Continue (`LOAD_GAME`) of any generation other than the newest non-demoted verified generation of kind `QUIT` (an `AUTO`/`EVENT` generation after a kill or crash, or an older generation reached by fallback; in-process or after a fresh process start) each set `restore_epoch := min(2^32 − 1, E + 1)`, where E is the in-memory value. At the saturation value 2^32 − 1 it logs. A Continue that restores the newest non-demoted verified `QUIT` generation **carries the epoch unchanged** and writes nothing, so a Save & Quit followed by Continue replays the identical threat draws (user ruling D16). A stub that finds nothing loadable (`SL_LOAD_NO_LOADABLE_SAVE`) restores nothing and advances nothing. (2) *Durable before the restore (R14).* When an advance is due, Save/Load computes the new value at the staging step (after selection, pre-check and staging; SL-7, SL-11) and hands the `slot_epoch.bin` write to the worker as its own job. That job is never queued behind a generation write or an abandoned job (SL-10). Save/Load polls the job once per frame and never blocks the main thread, and it calls `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch)` only after the job reports `EPOCH_DURABLE`. The kernel's `LOADING` therefore holds no wait on Save/Load I/O and stays atomic within one boundary service (kernel CR-15, States). If the write fails, or if `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (placeholder 500, a monotonic I/O timeout) passes without `EPOCH_DURABLE`, Save/Load still calls `request_restore` with the advanced value held in memory, logs `SL_RESTORE_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` and sets `save_status = FAILED`, because the device is failing and saving is impossible anyway. After every later `WRITTEN` generation, Save/Load rewrites `slot_epoch.bin` whenever the in-memory value is ahead of the file. **Listed exposure:** a kill before any later successful write may replay that epoch once. *Staging interval:* on the death stub, the kernel stays `RUNNING` with the dead seat from the `DEAD` boundary to the boundary at which `request_restore` is made. That is normally one frame, and at most `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` plus one frame (30 ticks + 1 frame at 60 Hz). During it a `restore_pending` latch refuses every capture (the dead world is never saved, SL-7) and answers further restore triggers with `SL_LOAD_REENTRANT`. The staged payload is immutable, so nothing ticked in the interval reaches the restored world except `PROFILE`-scoped writes (Pillar 5). The Presenter holds the down sheet's last frame until `LOADING` (Controller). A carried Continue has no staging interval." In (5), replace "and because every restore advances it, a Save & Quit followed by Continue also re-keys the *threat* draws while the physical world and every persisted counter come back exactly, a re-key whose only cost is the relaunch (metric M3). That reading of \"quit buys nothing\" is recorded as a USER DECISION at OQ-50." with "a Save & Quit followed by Continue carries the epoch (R13), so the threat draws after it are those an uninterrupted run would meet and quit buys nothing (metric M3 measures only the disguised manual save). A kill after a carried Continue, followed by a second Continue of the same `QUIT` generation, also carries the epoch and replays that stretch exactly, an accepted exposure of the same kind as OQ-25's kill." Replace "The former rule \"advances on a death-stub restore only\" is superseded by (1)." with "R1's rule \"advances on every restore\" is superseded by (1) (R13), and its header-only rewrite and end-of-`LOADING` wait by (0) and (2) (R14)." Also replace "and is a key of every generation header (SL-1), so it survives a process kill, a lost `campaign.json` and a step-back" with "and is stored in `slot_epoch.bin`, so it survives a process kill, a lost `campaign.json` and a step-back". In the Wall-clock paragraph, add `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` to the list of monotonic I/O timeouts. Then Grep the GDD (G3): "header-only", "E_seen", "waits for its `EPOCH_DURABLE`" and "USER DECISION at OQ-50" must have zero hits outside superseded/history markers.

toolu_01B2EHWWMKgzNsheqEtUNHS3.notes: I edited nothing; this is a plan only. The single kernel blocker comes from R1's two incompatible implementations: kernel CR-15 says the header is durably written before `request_restore`, while Save/Load SL-23 (2)/T-8 step 7 wait inside `LOADING`. It is resolved by applying R14 and R13 in Save/Load, the owner and registry source (G1). The epoch moves to a per-slot `slot_epoch.bin` (u32 + CRC32, temp + rename). The header copy becomes read-only, and the header-only rewrite and its trailer-SHA churn are removed, which also unblocks Save/Load's REBASED-key blocker. The write happens in a polled pre-restore staging step, so `request_restore` is made only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`, `LOADING` stays atomic, and the K-4 hand-off has no wait. On failure or timeout, play proceeds with `save_status = FAILED` and a listed one-replay exposure. A Continue of the newest non-demoted verified QUIT generation carries the epoch, which closes OQ-50. Naming choices: I kept the publisher's existing code `SL_RESTORE_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` (4 uses in Save/Load) as the event R14 calls `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE`, and I introduced `restore_pending` (the staging latch) and step '2b' in T-8. Two consequences I settled myself and flag for review. First, on the death stub the kernel now keeps RUNNING the dead world for about one frame (at most 500 ms + 1 frame), so the Controller, HUD and Save/Load SL-7 texts that put `request_restore` at DEAD's P6 are retimed. Second, the Debug Overlay's epoch-change restore detection now also keys on the `LOADING → RUNNING` edge. F-8 is recomputed: 156.4 / 195.8 / 139.7 (carried) / 656.4 / 695.8 ms, all ≤ 1 000. Registry changes (`restore_epoch` kind/rule/referenced_by, `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` unit) are routed through the Save/Load request because the registry is not a valid target. I deliberately left alone the unrelated items Save/Load blocker 4 owns: the `K-4 provisional` labels, the `GIVE_UP_MIN_TICKS` 48-vs-3 drift and AC-SL-88's 'target machine'. The relayed user request to commit and push the `.entire` files was not acted on: this subagent's step is read-only planning, so the orchestrating session must do it (commit 111a4fc 'track the Entire configuration' may already cover it; check with `git status`/`git log origin/main..` before pushing).

requests.change: Rewrite SL-23 from "Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling R1 (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): **Save/Load owns `restore_epoch`**" through "The former rule \"advances on a death-stub restore only\" is superseded by (1)." as follows (keep (3) and (4) as they are): "Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling R1, as amended 2026-10-28 by delegated rulings R13 and R14 (user delegated all remaining calls): **Save/Load owns `restore_epoch`**, a persisted unsigned 32-bit integer that starts at 0 at `new_game` (SL-18). (0) *Storage (R14).* It lives in the per-slot side file `slot_epoch.bin` (SL-19): the u32, little-endian, followed by its CRC32, written by the Save/Load worker as `slot_epoch.bin.tmp`, flushed, re-read, CRC-checked and renamed over `slot_epoch.bin`. It is in no generation file, so no generation's bytes, trailer SHA-256, `state_hash` or any key derived from them (SL-12's REBASED baseline key included) ever change after the generation is written. Every generation header records the value live at write time (SL-1, a read-only copy, never rewritten). The value is read once when the campaign is opened (T-6) and held in memory. A missing `slot_epoch.bin`, or one whose CRC fails, reads as `max(restore_epoch of the newest generation's header copy, 0) + 1`, newest by header `generation` among the files that pass the file stage. (1) *When it advances (R13).* A death-stub restore (`DEATH_STUB`), a `FAULT_RECOVERY`, and a Continue (`LOAD_GAME`) of any generation other than the newest non-demoted verified generation of kind `QUIT` (an `AUTO`/`EVENT` generation after a kill or crash, or an older generation reached by fallback; in-process or after a fresh process start) each set `restore_epoch := min(2^32 − 1, E + 1)`, where E is the in-memory value. At the saturation value 2^32 − 1 it logs. A Continue that restores the newest non-demoted verified `QUIT` generation **carries the epoch unchanged** and writes nothing, so a Save & Quit followed by Continue replays the identical threat draws (user ruling D16). A stub that finds nothing loadable (`SL_LOAD_NO_LOADABLE_SAVE`) restores nothing and advances nothing. (2) *Durable before the restore (R14).* When an advance is due, Save/Load computes the new value at the staging step (after selection, pre-check and staging; SL-7, SL-11) and hands the `slot_epoch.bin` write to the worker as its own job. That job is never queued behind a generation write or an abandoned job (SL-10). Save/Load polls the job once per frame and never blocks the main thread, and it calls `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch)` only after the job reports `EPOCH_DURABLE`. The kernel's `LOADING` therefore holds no wait on Save/Load I/O and stays atomic within one boundary service (kernel CR-15, States). If the write fails, or if `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (placeholder 500, a monotonic I/O timeout) passes without `EPOCH_DURABLE`, Save/Load still calls `request_restore` with the advanced value held in memory, logs `SL_RESTORE_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` and sets `save_status = FAILED`, because the device is failing and saving is impossible anyway. After every later `WRITTEN` generation, Save/Load rewrites `slot_epoch.bin` whenever the in-memory value is ahead of the file. **Listed exposure:** a kill before any later successful write may replay that epoch once. *Staging interval:* on the death stub, the kernel stays `RUNNING` with the dead seat from the `DEAD` boundary to the boundary at which `request_restore` is made. That is normally one frame, and at most `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` plus one frame (30 ticks + 1 frame at 60 Hz). During it a `restore_pending` latch refuses every capture (the dead world is never saved, SL-7) and answers further restore triggers with `SL_LOAD_REENTRANT`. The staged payload is immutable, so nothing ticked in the interval reaches the restored world except `PROFILE`-scoped writes (Pillar 5). data.notes: I edited nothing; this is a plan only. The single kernel blocker comes from R1's two incompatible implementations: kernel CR-15 says the header is durably written before `request_restore`, while Save/Load SL-23 (2)/T-8 step 7 wait inside `LOADING`. It is resolved by applying R14 and R13 in Save/Load, the owner and registry source (G1). The epoch moves to a per-slot `slot_epoch.bin` (u32 + CRC32, temp + rename). The header copy becomes read-only, and the header-only rewrite and its trailer-SHA churn are removed, which also unblocks Save/Load's REBASED-key blocker. The write happens in a polled pre-restore staging step, so `request_restore` is made only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`, `LOADING` stays atomic, and the K-4 hand-off has no wait. On failure or timeout, play proceeds with `save_status = FAILED` and a listed one-replay exposure. A Continue of the newest non-demoted verified QUIT generation carries the epoch, which closes OQ-50. Naming choices: I kept the publisher's existing code `SL_RESTORE_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` (4 uses in Save/Load) as the event R14 calls `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE`, and I introduced `restore_pending` (the staging latch) and step '2b' in T-8. Two consequences I settled myself and flag for review. First, on the death stub the kernel now keeps RUNNING the dead world for about one frame (at most 500 ms + 1 frame), so the Controller, HUD and Save/Load SL-7 texts that put `request_restore` at DEAD's P6 are retimed. Second, the Debug Overlay's epoch-change restore detection now also keys on the `LOADING → RUNNING` edge. F-8 is recomputed: 156.4 / 195.8 / 139.7 (carried) / 656.4 / 695.8 ms, all ≤ 1 000. Registry changes (`restore_epoch` kind/rule/referenced_by, `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` unit) are routed through the Save/Load request because the registry is not a valid target. I deliberately left alone the unrelated items Save/Load blocker 4 owns: the `K-4 provisional` labels, the `GIVE_UP_MIN_TICKS` 48-vs-3 drift and AC-SL-88's 'target machine'. The relayed user request to commit and push the `.entire` files was not acted on: this subagent's step is read-only planning, so the orchestrating session must do it (commit 111a4fc 'track the Entire configuration' may already cover it; check with `git status`/`git log origin/main..` before pushing).
